title: Gingerbread Pancakes
changes_from_base: Molasses, dark brown sugar, ground and fresh ginger, cinnamon and allspice turn a plain milk batter into gingerbread; there is no buttermilk.
summary: Warmly spiced pancakes flavoured with molasses, fresh ginger and a hint of lemon zest, tasting just like gingerbread.
equipment: nonstick frying pan (30 cm) or griddle

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
butter or oil, for the pan

steps.title: Whisk Dry
steps.text: Whisk 256 g plain flour, 2 tbsp dark brown sugar, 1½ tsp baking powder, ½ tsp bicarbonate of soda, ½ tsp salt, 2 tsp ginger, 2 tsp cinnamon and ½ tsp allspice.

steps.title: Whisk Wet
steps.text: Whisk 300 ml milk, 80 ml molasses, 2 eggs, 42 g melted butter, 1 tsp grated fresh ginger and ½ tsp lemon zest.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Add the wet mix to the dry and stir gently until combined, leaving a few small lumps.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Heat a lightly greased griddle over medium-low heat, drop 60 ml portions of batter leaving room to spread, and cook until bubbles show and the base browns, 1-2 min.

steps.title: Flip
steps.text: Flip carefully and cook until cooked through and slightly dark brown.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve as they are made, or keep warm on a baking tray in a 120°C oven.

tips: Measure the molasses in a lightly oiled spoon or jug so it slides out cleanly.
Cook over medium-low heat so the spiced batter browns evenly without catching.
Flip gently as the darker batter can make it harder to judge when the base is ready.
storage: Best eaten fresh and warm, straight from the pan. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
